idea.body: An angle of elevation is measured up from the ground to a point above it. An angle of depression is measured down from a height to a point below it. Both form a right triangle with a horizontal ground leg and a vertical height leg, so the same three ratios from trig ratios apply directly. A drone hovers above a rover with a ground distance of 12 meters. The angle of elevation from the rover to the drone is 45 degrees. Tangent of 45 degrees is 1, so the height equals the ground distance, 12 meters. A different angle needs the matching ratio, sine, cosine or tangent, for whichever two sides are known and unknown.

figure.alt: A right triangle showing a ground distance of 12 and a height of 12, the angle of elevation marked at the ground vertex.

workedExample.prompt: A rocket tracked from a control room is 41 meters away along the line of sight. The angle of elevation has sine 40/41. Find the ground distance to the rocket.
steps: Sine 40/41 names the height leg and the line of sight: height is 40, line of sight is 41.
The ground distance is the third side of that right triangle, the leg still missing.
By the Pythagorean theorem, 41 squared minus 40 squared is 81, and the square root of 81 is 9.

figure.alt: A right triangle showing a ground distance of 9 and a height of 40, the angle of elevation marked at the ground vertex.

ways.name: Set up the triangle and match the ratio
ways.when: Use this any time an elevation or depression angle is given with one side.
steps: A drone hovers above a robot with a ground distance of 9 meters.
The angle of elevation forms a right triangle: ground leg, height leg, line of sight as hypotenuse.
The angle of elevation, 45 degrees, sits at the ground vertex.
Height and ground distance are opposite and adjacent to that angle, so tangent connects them.
Tangent of 45 degrees is 1, so height equals ground distance: 9 meters.
ways.example: A drone hovers above a robot with a ground distance of 9 meters. The angle of elevation is 45 degrees. Find the height.
ways.trap: Using sine or cosine instead of tangent when only the two legs, not the hypotenuse, are involved.

figure.alt: A right triangle with ground leg and height leg both 9 meters, the 45 degree angle marked at the ground vertex.

frames.caption: Drone above robot, ground distance 9 m.
Right triangle: ground, height, line of sight
45 degree angle sits at the ground vertex

ways.name: Depression equals elevation across the parallel
ways.when: Use this when the angle is given as a depression, looking down from a height.
steps: A drone hovers 12 meters above a robot, with a 30 degree angle of depression to it.
The drone's horizontal path and the ground are two parallel horizontal lines.
The line of sight is a transversal, so the depression and elevation angles are equal alternate angles.
Treat the ground triangle with a 30 degree angle of elevation instead.
Tangent of 30 degrees is sqrt(3)/3, so distance is 12 divided by that ratio: 12 sqrt(3).
ways.example: A drone hovers 12 meters above a robot. The angle of depression to the robot is 30 degrees. Find the horizontal distance to the robot.
ways.trap: Treating the angle of depression as if it were already measured at the ground point.

figure.alt: Two parallel horizontal lines with a drone point on top and a robot point below, the line of sight making equal 30 degree angles.

frames.caption: Drone D above, robot R below.
Drone 12 m up, 30 degree depression to R
Drone path & ground are parallel lines

ways.name: Read a ratio, find the missing side
ways.when: Use this when a ratio is given directly instead of a whole degree angle.
steps: A rocket's line of sight from a tracking station is 25 meters.
Cosine of the angle of elevation is 24/25: 24 is the ground leg, 25 is the line of sight.
Height is the third side of that right triangle, the leg still missing.
By the Pythagorean theorem, 25 squared minus 24 squared is 625 minus 576, which is 49.
The square root of 49 is 7, so the height is 7 meters.
ways.example: A rocket's line of sight is 25 meters. Cosine of the angle of elevation is 24/25. Find the height.
ways.trap: Treating the given ratio as the answer instead of solving for the missing side.

figure.alt: A right triangle with ground leg 24 meters and height 7 meters, hypotenuse 25 meters, angle A marked.

frames.caption: Line of sight 25 m; cos A = 24/25.
Height is the missing third side

bank.prompt: A drone climbing away from a rover sights a point at an angle of elevation of 45 degrees. The ground distance to the point is 12 meters. Find the height of the point above the ground.
explanation: At 45 degrees, the height leg and the ground leg of the right triangle are equal, because tangent of 45 degrees is 1.
So the missing distance equals the one that is given: 12 meters.
hints: Tangent of 45 degrees has one exact value; what is it?
If tangent is 1, what does that say about the two legs of the right triangle?
bank.socraticHint: What is tangent of 45 degrees exactly?
bank.useAgain: when an angle of elevation or depression is exactly 45 degrees.
